title: Compatibility Handoff Bridge for VPC/on‑prem Upgrades
creator: Mei Chen
description: Build a lightweight Compatibility Handoff Bridge component that sits between the Redwood control plane and customer-managed Private agents (VPC/on-prem). The bridge's purpose is to mediate upgrade handoffs and orchestrated migrations with minimal assumptions about outbound connectivity, provide a pluggable validation/step interface (schema migrations, config transforms, binary compatibility checks), and enforce rollout gates across LTS channels and cohort cohorts. Key constraints: must support air-gapped environments via push/pull bundles, enable dry-run mode with snapshotting, and provide automated rollback triggers when health checks fail. This ticket covers design, a PoC implementation, integration tests against the private-agent simulator, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and signed off by Release Engineering and Security (link in related_links)
PoC bridge can perform a staged schema migration with dry-run and commit phases against the simulator (no data loss)
Bridge exposes a migration step API and validator hook; at least three validators implemented: schema, protobuf compatibility, and config-set sanity
Support for LTS channel tagging and cohort assignment in rollout plan; can route 5%/25%/100% staged releases
Automatic rollback policy triggers on defined health regression signals (latency, error-rate, token-error-rate) and can be executed from Console or CLI
Telemetry and audit events emitted to the Console for every handoff step (timestamps, step result, agent-id, snapshot id)
Security review completed and allowed for private deployments (KMS/HSM metadata not exported)
Runbook and step-by-step migration playbook added to runbooks; one dry-run executed and documented
notes_and_progress:
2026-02-18: Ticket created by Mei Chen. Initial problem statement and constraints captured.
2026-02-22: Architecture sketch completed — bridge is a small stateful controller that accepts signed bundles, validates locally, and coordinates staged rollouts with agent acknowledgements. Sketch link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Compat+Handoff+Bridge
2026-02-26: Design review with Release Eng and Security. Security requested that metadata never leaves customer VPC unless explicitly permitted; we agreed on an opt-in telemetry handshake. Action: add encryption envelope for bundle and KMS integration.
2026-03-02: PoC lab: implemented bundle format and local validator harness. Verified dry-run for schema migration against simulator. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/7890
2026-03-05: Integration tests failing intermittently under network partition simulation (simulator). Root cause: agent acknowledgement timeout not resilient to transient clock skew. Added ack backoff and idempotent replay logic.
2026-03-09: Demo with Solutions Eng showed staged rollout working (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on synthetic error injected by health probe. Recorded demo and linked in related_links.
Open items: add protobuf compatibility checker as a compiled validator, finalize telemetry fields with Observability team, add canary cohort selection policy to Console UI.
Blockers: Security sign-off pending for KMS/HSM metadata flow; reach out to security reviewer (Liam O'Connor) for final OK.
